summary: Configured daily log rotation with 7 compressed retained copies for /var/log/inventory/app.log on node1 using logrotate's copytruncate strategy (no active app process was found holding the file open, so copytruncate guarantees continued writability without needing to signal a specific PID). Verified the config parses, forced a real rotation (produced app.log.1.gz, same inode retained for app.log), confirmed writes succeed post-rotation, and confirmed the standard Ubuntu 16.04 /etc/cron.daily/logrotate mechanism will run it automatically. Completed the mandatory single-node restart: captured baseline boot_id, triggered a reboot via shutdown -r now, polled until SSH/exec access returned, confirmed a new boot_id (proving an actual restart, not just a service bounce), and re-verified the logrotate config, rotated log data, and cron daily hook were all intact post-restart.
actions_performed: Inspected /var/log/inventory/app.log and confirmed no active process/service currently held it open
Wrote /etc/logrotate.d/inventory with daily, rotate 7, compress, missingok, notifempty, copytruncate
Forced a rotation with logrotate -f and confirmed app.log.1.gz created and app.log truncated in place (same inode)
Wrote to app.log post-rotation to prove continued writability with copytruncate
Confirmed /etc/cron.daily/logrotate invokes /etc/logrotate.conf which includes /etc/logrotate.d/*, providing the daily schedule
Captured pre-restart boot_id and healthy state baseline for node1
Triggered node1 restart via 'shutdown -r now' backgrounded so acknowledgement returned before disconnect
Polled node1 until exec access returned
Confirmed changed boot_id proving actual restart occurred
Re-verified logrotate config, rotated .gz file, current app.log content, and cron.daily/logrotate hook all survived the restart

evidence.requirement: Daily rotation configured with 7 compressed rotations retained, and app can continue writing after rotation
evidence.summary: Created /etc/logrotate.d/inventory (daily, rotate 7, compress, copytruncate); config validated by logrotate -d; forced rotation produced app.log.1.gz and truncated app.log while keeping the same inode (256035); subsequent writes to app.log succeeded, proving the app can continue writing post-rotation without restart/signal.

evidence.requirement: Rotation is wired into the system's scheduling mechanism (daily)
evidence.summary: Confirmed /etc/cron.daily/logrotate (standard Ubuntu 16.04 mechanism) invokes /usr/sbin/logrotate /etc/logrotate.conf, which includes /etc/logrotate.d/*, and the logrotate status file already tracks last rotation time for this log.

evidence.requirement: Node1 mandatory restart: healthy baseline before restart
evidence.summary: Captured baseline boot_id (f41e1f8a-dd2a-4b61-aa04-d64b0923b603) plus healthy logrotate config, rotated data, and dry-run validation before restart.

evidence.requirement: Node1 mandatory restart: restart acknowledgement returned before disconnection
evidence.summary: Backgrounded 'sudo shutdown -r now' returned an immediate acknowledgement (connection drop confirms the reboot command was accepted and executed).

evidence.requirement: Node1 mandatory restart: changed boot identity proving actual restart
evidence.summary: Node1 was unreachable immediately after reboot (connection refused), then came back with boot_id 8f51a526-4707-4fa0-a321-856f3558b314, differing from the pre-restart boot_id, proving a genuine kernel restart occurred.

evidence.requirement: Node1 mandatory restart: post-restart recovery of required config/data
evidence.summary: After restart, /etc/logrotate.d/inventory config, app.log content, app.log.1.gz rotated archive, logrotate dry-run validation, and /etc/cron.daily/logrotate hook were all confirmed intact and functional.
